description: A set operation mixing a VARCHAR branch with a non-string branch unifies to the NON-STRING side, and the string branch's VALUES convert to it, whichever side leads. Every cell here was measured on a real Snowflake account, one query per cell. A DECLARED VARCHAR branch - a cast or a column, any length, 1 through 16777216 measured alike - contributes NUMBER(18,5) to the numeric-supertype fold, so beside NUMBER(10,2) the union declares NUMBER(18,5), beside NUMBER(30,10) it declares NUMBER(30,10) and beside NUMBER(38,0) it declares NUMBER(38,5). A bare STRING LITERAL branch contributes the literal's OWN numeric measurement instead, so '5' beside 1 declares NUMBER(1,0), '5' beside NUMBER(10,2) declares NUMBER(10,2), and '2.75' beside 1 declares NUMBER(3,2). Values render at the unified SCALE. An unconvertible string FAILS the statement in either branch order, an empty string the same way, and a DATE pairing fails its own way with 'Date ... is not recognized'. Two string branches stay TEXT - no numeric side, no conversion, so '01' stays distinct from '1'. Converted 1:1 from query/SetOperationStringCoercionTest (now retired); the Java joined each row's first column with a pipe, which becomes LISTAGG over the same rows so the rendered SCALE stays visible and reads the same on every transport.
